answer: A reputation garden works like this: every agent starts as a tiny ember with almost no trust, and only earns more by doing verifiable work that peers can check on the horizon of future rounds. A Sybil attacker can spawn thousands of fresh identities, but each one starts at zero reputation and must pay the same slow cost of real, attested work before it can influence anything — so flooding the network buys no power, only a long, expensive climb.
